MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD
SUBJECT: LD 159 An Act to Require Vehicle Registrations to Include the Next of Kin of the Vehicle Owner

22 Feb 25

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Committee Transportation,
1. Thank you for allowing me to introduce my bill, LD 159 An Act to Require Vehicle Registrations to Include the Next of Kin of the Vehicle Owner. This is a simple bill - as written it requires that a vehicle that is registered to an individual include information about the registered owner's next of kin.
2. I was asked to sponsor this bill by another member of the law enforcement profession, but having been introduced to the bill I honestly wish I had thought of it sooner.
3. I served as a law enforcement officer in the State of Maine for 17 years in three municipal departments and I want to share with you three different types of scenarios that I personally encountered during that time where this would have been extremely helpful in furthering public safety.
4. There were instances when I responded to motor vehicle crashes that involved fatalities where a notification of the victims family was delayed because the driver was from out of town, unknown to us and was the only name on the registration. This required huge amounts of investigative work to identify someone in the decedent's family to notify, sometimes taking many hours. The need for a prompt death notification is often exasperated by the fact that information gleaned from `scannerland' is often posted on social media and family members sometimes find out about motor vehicle deaths improperly before a law enforcement agency can make a proper notification. Additionally, even without a death, in the case of a serious accident where the driver might be disabled or incapacitated,

being able to make a prompt contact with family is vital. And while I have not experienced this scenario personally, in a scenario where a driver with an unknown contact is a candidate for organ donation prompt contact is also extremely important, as every minute counts.
5. In my second scenario, which I and many other LEOs have encountered, it has happened that we have encountered elderly drivers in an altered mental state, specifically someone who is suffering from dementia or Alzheimer's. Often, these people are far from home haven gotten disoriented and haven driven some distance, and often they are the only registered owner listed. If a Silver Alert has not yet been issued, it is often very difficult to immediately locate a relative.
6. In my final scenario, again which I have encountered, is when a law enforcement officer encounters what is known in our parlance as a 10-48, or `Unattended Death'. While this is the least common scenario, at least in my experience, it does happen. And even though the protocol is to notify the Medical Examiner when encountering an unattended death, if the person in the vehicle is unknown to us, not a local, and the only registered owner listed, it can be problematic locating someone for additional notifications.
7. After submitting this bill I was notified by a representative of the Probate Courts and informed that the term `Next of Kin' had a specific legal meaning and was asked if I would be agreeable to amending the bill by changing the term Next of Kin to Emergency Contact. As I believe this would still accomplish the intent of the bill, I would be very agreeable to this.
8. I also understand that there would obviously be some cost to the State if this change is made. Not only would the software that processes vehicle registrations have to be changed by adding fields for the added data, but the physical forms that the registrations are printed on would also have to be changed. I believe that the public safety benefit outweighs the cost of the change to the software. However I believe that the costs for form changes can be minimized by either using existing forms and printing the new field information in some of the blank space on the right hand side of the paper registrations until the current stock of forms is depleted or by setting an implementation date based on the current stock of existing paper registration forms and their estimated date of depletion.
9. I respectfully encourage the committee to consider this legislation with a vote of `Ought To Pass'.
Respectfully,

Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Opposition To
LD 159- An Act to Require Vehicle Registrations to Include the Next of Kin of the Vehicle Owner
February 27, 2025
Sen. Nangle, Rep. Crafts, and distinguished members of the Transportation Committee, my name is Rebecca Graham, and I am submitting testimony in opposition to LD 159 at the direction of MMA's Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). Our LPC is made up of individuals from across Maine with municipal officials elected by their peers across Maine's 35 Senate districts representing communities with very different access to available enforcement resources and local capacity.
Officials are concerned that this requirement poses unnecessary bureaucratic hoops for individuals who have no direct next of kin to designate another, while respecting there is a desire to provide an easily accessible contact for individuals involved in a fatal or life-threatening accident. As drafted, the bill would require every individual to identify someone who later is not the desired choice of the individual to be considered a next of kin and may require an individual to continually update a system when they have no family members. The provision should be voluntary for all individuals who renew a registration and often has no nexus to the individual operator of a motor vehicle which may cause unnecessary distress for the vehicle owner.
Because such a designation would offer a false sense of belief that the operator may also be the registered owner, officials believe that such a requirement may be better suited as a voluntary disclose for the driver's license program and not the vehicle registration program. Municipal officials often register vehicles on behalf of registered owners presented by a party who is registering a vehicle on behalf of the owner and may lead to the designation either being mistakenly assigned to another individual or place additional barrier for individuals who are not able to be present to register their vehicle and the ability to assign the task to another trusted party while they are abroad serving the military or attending college, etc.
Additionally, the added collection and continual updating of information regarding the next of kin during the registration process will constitute an added duty for municipal clerks and this bill will need the mandate preamble. Once a vehicle is registered currently, there is no reason to reopen the file until the following year or until the vehicle is transferred to a new owner, or new municipality. As drafted, municipal clerks will also be charged with continually updating the designation as family or friendship dynamics change unless there is a system established for self-reporting through the Bureau of Motor Vehicles. Not all communities are connected to the automated online registration system.
For these reasons, municipal officials ask that you consider assigning the task to licensing authority not municipal vehicle registration clerks and attach the next of kin designation to a task that requires often requires an in person renewal rather than place additional barriers or processes to registering a motor vehicle, which may have no nexus to the vehicle operation.

L.D. 159 "An Act to Require Vehicle Registrations to Include the Next of Kin of the Vehicle

Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State
Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles
February 27, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation,
my name is Shenna Bellows. I am the Secretary of State and I reside in Manchester. I am providing testimony in opposition to L.D. 159 "An Act to Require Vehicle Registrations to Include the Next of Kin
of the Vehicle Owner."
This bill would require the Secretary of State to add the legal name and address of the next of kin of the
registrant, if the registrant is an individual, to all registration documents. Should this bill pass, the workload and fiscal note will be substantial. This bill would require all registration forms to be updated.
Multiple BMV computer systems and the municipal computer systems would also need to be updated.
Every time an update is required to the municipal computer systems the vendors increase their maintenance fees.
The purpose of a registration document is not to identify someone's next of kin. Registration certificates are used to help determine vehicle ownership, provide data when tracking a criminal, or assessing taxes.
While the intent of this bill is to identify next of kin in the tragic incidence when a death notification is required, it is important to remember that someone other than the registrant could be driving the vehicle. Also, up to three (3) individuals may be listed on a registration. This means someone other than a vehicle
owner may be listed on the registration. Each of the individuals are considered a registrant. A vehicle
owner may authorize someone else to register the vehicle in certain circumstances. Also, if a registrant's right to register a motor vehicle is suspended due to an OUI, the registrant's name may be removed from
the registration and put into a family men1ber's name, if they reside in the same household until their
right to register is restored.
This raises many questions regarding implementation of L.D. 159. For example, if there is more than one
individual on a registration, will a next of kin be required for each registrant? If there are 3 individuals on
a registration, the next of kin could be different for everyone. This means we could potentially have 6
names with different addresses on a registration document and the registration would need to specify which next of kin is designated for each registrant.

Processing time for registration will be significantly increased for municipalities and BMV branches. We
will also be processing more corrected registrations than we do now, as each time next of kin changes for
one registrant, the registration document would need to be updated. Another question raised by this bill is whether or not someone would need to consent to being the next of
kin on a registration. If so, we would have to collect each person's signature, which may require a new
form to be created. Additionally, this bill does not address what would happen if someone doesn't have a next of kin. Nor does it address whether next of kin would be required on registrations that are issued to protected registrants, for example, registrants in the Address Confidentiality Program because they have been victims of domestic abuse, sexual assault or stalking?
This is not an issue that requires a new law. The easiest Way to solve this matter is to remind people to keep emergency contact information on them. For example,most people carry cell phones and can mark
their emergency contacts as such in their contacts. Thank you for your time and I would be happy to answer your questions.
